'''George Russell Lakey''' (born November 2, 1937) is an activist, [[sociologist]], and writer who added academic underpinning to the concept of [[nonviolent revolution]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Book Review: Of Gravlax and Power Grids|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2016-07-07/book-review-of-gravlax-and-power-grids|publisher=Bloomberg L.P.|accessdate=12 December 2017|date=7 July 2016}}</ref> He also refined the practice of experiential training for activists which he calls "Direct Education".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://daryncambridge.com/2010/12/17/key-insights-from-george-lakeys-book-facilitating-group-learning/ |title=Key Insights from George Lakey's book, "Facilitating Group Learning" &#124; Daryn R. Cambridge |publisher=Daryncambridge.com |date=17 December 2010 |accessdate=3 December 2016}}</ref> A [[Quaker]], he has co-founded and led numerous organizations and campaigns for justice and peace.<ref name="afsc.org">{{cite web|url=https://www.afsc.org/friends/preaching-peace-and-justice-interview-george-lakey|title=Preaching Peace and Justice: An Interview with George Lakey|date=9 April 2012|work=afsc.org|accessdate=3 December 2016}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Lakey was born to Dora M. and Russell George Lakey, a [[slate industry|slate]] miner, in [[Bangor, Pennsylvania]].<ref name="swarthmore.edu">{{cite web|url=http://bulletin.swarthmore.edu/bulletin-issue-archive/archive_p=217.html|title=Rebel Energy – Swarthmore College Bulletin|work=swarthmore.edu|accessdate=3 December 2016}}</ref> He was identified as a prospective [[child preacher]] for his church, and at age 12, he gave a sermon promoting [[racial equality]] as the will of God, although his sermon was not well received at the time.<ref name="rushe2019">{{cite news
|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2019/mar/03/civil-rights-legend-george-lakey-this-is-a-bigger-opportunity-than-the-60s
|last=Rushe|first=Dominic
|date=March 3, 2019
|title=Civil rights legend George Lakey on how progressives can win
|work=[[The Guardian]]
|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20190303201344/https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2019/mar/03/civil-rights-legend-george-lakey-this-is-a-bigger-opportunity-than-the-60s|archivedate=March 3, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>  He graduated from [[Cheyney University]] in [[Cheyney, Pennsylvania]], and also studied at the [[University of Oslo]] in Norway. There he married Berit Mathiesen in 1960 and taught at an [[Oslo]] high school. He continued his sociology studies at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] in [[Philadelphia]], earning a [[master's degree]] and completing coursework for a [[Ph.D.]] but never completing it.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/corvallis-gazette-times-westminster-hous/191352137/ |title=Westminster House Seminar -- Change Without Violence? |work=[[Corvallis Gazette-Times]] |date=January 23, 1971 |via=newspapers.com }}</ref><ref name=Corr1987>{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-philadelphia-inquirer-for-peace-work/191352381/ |title=A Lifelong Warrior For Peace |last=Corr |first=John |work=[[Philadelphia Inquirer]] |date=November 29, 1987 |pages=[https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-philadelphia-inquirer-a-lifelong-war/191352481/ 1-J],[https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-philadelphia-inquirer-for-peace-work/191352381/ 9-J] |via=newspapers.com |id={{Proquest|1831747110}} }}</ref>

==Career==
===Activism===
In the late 1950s, Lakey was active in the [[Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament|ban-the-bomb movement]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.quakerranter.org/tag/george-lakey/|title=George Lakey – Quaker Ranter|work=quakerranter.org|accessdate=3 December 2016}}</ref> then participated in the [[civil rights movement]], in 1963 being arrested in a sit-in.<ref name="afsc.org"/> The following year he was a trainer for [[Mississippi Freedom Summer]] and co-authored his first book, ''A Manual for Direct Action'', which was widely used in the South by the [[civil rights movement]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pendlehill.org/product/nonviolent-action-works/|title=Nonviolent Action: How It Works – Pendle Hill Quaker Books & Pamphlets|work=pendlehill.org|accessdate=3 December 2016}}</ref> In 1966 he co-founded the national body [[A Quaker Action Group]] (AQAG), whose activities took him in 1967 to [[Vietnam]] to participate in the sailing ship Phoenix's protest action in [[South Vietnam]] seeking to give medical supplies to the anti-war [[Buddhist]] movement there.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.atlasobscura.com/articles/the-american-boat-that-sailed-to-vietnam-during-the-warthen-disappeared|title=How a Modest Wooden Boat Became an International Icon During the Vietnam War, Then Disappeared|date=11 October 2016|work=atlasobscura.com|accessdate=3 December 2016}}</ref>

In 1970, Lakey was active within AQAG in the successful direct action in the [[Puerto Rico|Puerto Rican]] struggle to stop the [[U.S. Navy]] from using the island of [[Culebra, Puerto Rico|Culebra]] for target practice.<ref name="swarthmore.edu1">{{cite web|url=https://nvdatabase.swarthmore.edu/content/puerto-ricans-expel-united-states-navy-culebra-island-1970-1974|title=Puerto Ricans expel United States Navy from Culebra Island, 1970–1974 – Global Nonviolent Action Database|work=swarthmore.edu|accessdate=3 December 2016}}</ref> In 1971 he helped found [[Movement for a New Society]] (MNS), a network of autonomous groups working for a [[nonviolent revolution]].<ref name="lokashakti.org">{{cite web|url=http://www.lokashakti.org/encyclopedia/groups/831-movement-for-a-new-society|title=Movement for a New Society – Lokashakti Encyclopedia|work=lokashakti.org|accessdate=3 December 2016|archive-date=December 13, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171213084516/http://www.lokashakti.org/encyclopedia/groups/831-movement-for-a-new-society|url-status=dead}}</ref> The network featured living collectives and [[co-ops]] as well as participation in national movements of the 1970s and '80s. The network's training program at the ''[[Philadelphia]] Life Center Association'' became highly influential in the US and abroad in spreading [[Paulo Freire]]'s [[Popular education]] and other participatory training methods.<ref name="mayfirst.org">{{cite web|url=http://anarchiststudies.mayfirst.org/node/292|title=Anarchism and the Movement for a New Society: Direct Action and Prefigurative Community in the 1970s and 80s By Andrew Cornell – The Institute for Anarchist Studies|work=mayfirst.org|accessdate=3 December 2016|archive-date=December 25, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171225012859/http://anarchiststudies.mayfirst.org/node/292|url-status=dead}}</ref>

During the 1970s, he also gave national leadership to the ''Campaign to Stop the [[Rockwell B-1 Lancer|B-1 Bomber]] and Promote Peace Conversion,''<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.clarityfacilitation.com/papers/george.htm|title=Spirit in Conflict: George Lakey|work=clarityfacilitation.com|accessdate=3 December 2016}}</ref> which succeeded in persuading [[United States Congress|Congress]] and [[Jimmy Carter|President Carter]] to de-fund this Air Force program.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thestreetspirit.org/the-occupy-movement-stands-at-the-crossroads-street-spirit-interview-with-george-lakey-4/|title=The Occupy Movement Stands at the Crossroads: Street Spirit Interview with George Lakey|date=8 March 2012|work=thestreetspirit.org|accessdate=3 December 2016}}</ref> In 1976 he co-organized Men Against [[Patriarchy]], a pioneering anti-[[sexism]] movement for men. In 1982 he organized the [[Pennsylvania]] section of a national labor/community coalition named "Jobs with Peace" and directed that effort for seven years.<ref name="auto">Spirituality, Religion, and Peace Education, By Edward J. Brantmeier, Jing Lin, INFORMATION AGE PUBLISHING, John P. Miller, pg 90</ref>

In 1973, Lakey came out in public as a gay man, and joined the [[LGBT movement]], becoming part of what he later would call "[[Gay Liberation]]'s early visionary days."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wagingnonviolence.org/feature/lessons-from-the-lgbt-equality-movement/|title=Lessons from the LGBT equality movement – Waging Nonviolence|work=wagingnonviolence.org|date=2 April 2013 |accessdate=3 December 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://wagingnonviolence.org/feature/white-allies-can-learn-allies-gay-rights-struggle/|title=What white allies can learn from allies in the gay rights struggle|work=wagingnonviolence.org|date=4 July 2015 |accessdate=3 December 2016}}</ref>

In 1991, he co-founded with [[Philadelphia]] activist [[Barbara Smith]], Training for Change (TfC). Building on previous training at the [[Martin Luther King Jr.]] School for Social Change and [[Movement for a New Society]], Training for Change developed a new [[pedagogy]] called "Direct Education". Training for Change did trainings and consultations for activists and nongovernmental organizations in 20 countries.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=rRNWZ-YV1J8C&q=George+Lakey++%22Training+for+Change%22++%22+Movement+for+a+New+Society%22&pg=PA63|title=Oppose and Propose!: Lessons from Movement for a New Society|first=Andrew|last=Cornell|date=1 January 2011|publisher=AK Press|isbn=9781849350662|accessdate=3 December 2016|via=Google Books}}</ref>

In 2009, Lakey co-founded Earth Quaker Action Team (EQAT), to build a just and sustainable economy through nonviolent direct action campaigns. The group won its first campaign, forcing [[PNC Bank]] to stop financing [[mountaintop removal]] coal mining in [[Appalachia]]. In that campaign, while in his seventies, Lakey was arrested and also led a 200-mile march.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nvdatabase.swarthmore.edu/content/earth-quaker-action-team-campaigns-against-pnc-bank-financing-mountaintop-removal-coal-minin|title=Earth Quaker Action Team Campaigns Against PNC Bank for Financing Mountaintop Removal Coal Mining 2010–2015 – Global Nonviolent Action Database|work=swarthmore.edu|accessdate=3 December 2016}}</ref>

===Academia===
Lakey's first teaching post in higher education was in the Martin Luther King Jr. School of Social Change, a division of [[Crozer Theological Seminary]] in [[Chester, Pennsylvania]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://beautiful-business-llc.ticketleap.com/georgelakey/details|title=Talk and Book Signing – "Viking Economics"|work=ticketleap.com|accessdate=3 December 2016}}</ref> Lakey helped formulate the curriculum and then taught there for its first four years, 1965–1969.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nzetc.victoria.ac.nz/tm/scholarly/tei-Salient35241972-t1-body-d11.html|title=Pacifists' Visit – NZETC|work=victoria.ac.nz|accessdate=3 December 2016}}</ref> In this period he systematized the field of "Experiential Nonviolence Training" and the students were supported in efforts to connect field training with theory in [[direct action]]s.<ref>{{cite web|title=Satyagraha Foundation " Blog Archive " Nonviolent Peace Training as a Means of Linking Research and Action|url=https://www.satyagrahafoundation.org/nonviolent-peace-training-as-a-means-of-linking-research-and-action/|website=satyagrahafoundation.org|accessdate=12 December 2017}}</ref>

He joined the Peace Studies program at the [[University of Pennsylvania]], successfully expanding its undergraduate offerings and the participation of minority students. In addition, he helped lead a University of Pennsylvania group dynamics lab promoting innovative [[feminist]] leadership. He also taught [[peace studies]] at [[Haverford College]] in [[Haverford, Pennsylvania]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/citizens-voice-peace-activist-will-spea/191352798/ |title=Peace Activist Will Speak |work=[[Citizens' Voice]] |date=August 18, 1984 |via=newspapers.com }}</ref>

He later taught at [[Temple University]] and much later he accepted the endowed ''Eugene M. Lang Visiting Professorship in Issues of Social Change'' at [[Swarthmore College]]. He continued at [[Swarthmore College]] in [[Swarthmore, Pennsylvania]] as a Lang Professor and then as a research professor until his retirement.<ref name=Hopkins2024>{{cite news |title=West Philly peacekeeper continues mission: Documentary explores George Lakey's life devoted to peace, nonviolent protest |last=Hopkins |first=Earl |work=[[Philadelphia Daily News]] |date=October 24, 2024 |page=20 |id={{Proquest|3119916008}} }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://pcs.domains.swarthmore.edu/pcs/appreciation-of-george-lakey/ |title=Appreciation of George Lakey |website=pcs.domains.swarthmore.edu |publisher=[[Swarthmore College]] Department of Peace & Conflict Studies  |date=May 1, 2009 |access-date=February 15, 2026 }}</ref>

In 2010, Lakey was named by the ''National [[Peace and Justice Studies Association]]'' as "Peace Educator of the Year".

== Works ==
*''A Manual for Direct Action: Strategy and Tactics for Civil Rights and All Other Nonviolent Protest Movements'', co-author with Martin Oppenheimer; Chicago IL: [[Quadrangle Books]], 1965
*''In Place of War: Moving toward a New Society'', co-author with the [[American Friends Service Committee]] working party; lead author: James E. Bristol) New York City NY: [[Grossman Publishers|Grossman]], 1967
*''A Manifesto for Nonviolent Revolution: Toward a Just World Order, Vol. 1'' [[Boulder, Colorado|Boulder]] CO: [[Westview Press]], 1982 (originally published by [[War Resisters International]] (WRI) in 1972)
*''Strategy for a Living Revolution: a World Order Book''; New York City: [[Grossman Publishers|Grossman]], and San Francisco CA: [[W.H. Freeman]], 1973
**Revised and published as ''Powerful Peacemaking'', Philadelphia, PA: [[New Society Publishers]], 1987
**Revised and published as ''Toward a Living Revolution'', London, England: [[Peace News]], 2013, then published with the same title in a North American edition by [[Wipf & Stock]], 2016 (The central thesis of the above book on nonviolent revolution is found in "A Manifesto for Nonviolent Revolution" also by George Lakey and released by [[War Resisters International]] (WRI), 1975 (see above).)<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xmlWr4aAt4EC&q=George+Lakey+%22Strategy+for+a+Living+Revolution%22++%22A+Manifesto+for+Nonviolent+Revolution%22&pg=PA434|title=Protest, Power, and Change: An Encyclopedia of Nonviolent Action from ACT-UP to Women's Suffrage|first=Roger Powers|last=S|date=12 November 2012|publisher=Routledge|isbn=9781136764820|accessdate=3 December 2016|via=Google Books}}</ref>
*''Leadership for Change, Towards a Feminist Model'' (co-author with Bruce Kokopeli), Philadelphia, PA: [[New Society Publishers]], no date
*''Moving toward a New Society'' (co-author), Philadelphia, PA: New Society Publishers, 1975  
*''No Turning Back: Lesbian and Gay Liberation in the ‘80s'' (co-author with Erika Thorne), Philadelphia, PA: [[New Society Publishers]], 1983 
*''Grassroots and Nonprofit Leadership: A Guide for Organizations in Changing Times'' (co-author with Berit Lakey, Rod Napier, and Janice Robinson), Philadelphia, PA: [[New Society Publishers]], 1995; new edition (self-published), 2016; also published in translation in Cairo, Belgrade, and Bangkok
*''Opening Space for Democracy: Curriculum and Manual for Training for Third Party Nonviolent Intervention''; co-author with Daniel Hunter), Philadelphia, PA: Training for Change, 2004  
*''Facilitating Group Learning: Strategies for Success with Diverse Adult Learners.'' San Francisco CA: [[Jossey-Bass]], 2010  
*''Viking Economics: How the Scandinavians got it right and how we can, too''; New York, NY and London, England: [[Melville House Publishing]], 2016
*''How We Win: A Guide to Nonviolent Direct Action Campaigning''; New York, NY and London, England: [[Melville House Publishing]], 2018
*''Dancing with History: A Life for Peace and Justice''; New York, NY: [[Seven Stories Press]], 2022

Internet Development and Writing:
*''Global Nonviolent Action Database'', internet – ongoing;<ref>{{cite web | url=https://wagingnonviolence.org/2011/09/global-nonviolent-action-database-launched/ | title=Global Nonviolent Action Database launched | work=Waging Nonviolence | date=22 September 2011 | accessdate=20 May 2018 | author=Butigan, Ken }}</ref> over 1,000 researched cases from nearly 200 countries with focus on campaigns back to [[ancient Egypt]] that used [[nonviolent direct action]]. Searchable, and includes a narrative for each case.  Developed by Lakey with Swarthmore College and other university students, with Swarthmore's Peace and Conflict Studies, the Peace Collection, and the Lang Center for Civic and Social Responsibility.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nvdatabase.swarthmore.edu/content/who-made-database|title=Who made the database? – Global Nonviolent Action Database|work=swarthmore.edu|accessdate=3 December 2016}}</ref>
*''Waging Nonviolence'', an ongoing on-line blog where Lakey has been a regular featured columnist since 2010.
